newsitem.title: USA: Lilly says in deal with Cambridge Antibody.
newsitem.headline: Lilly says in deal with Cambridge Antibody.

text.p: Eli Lilly and Co said it entered into a collaborative research agreement with Cambridge Antibody Technology.

Lilly said it will get a license to Cambridge's large human single-chain antibody libraries and associated technologies for research, as well as options to develop antibody-based therapeutics and diagnostics.
In return, Cambridge will receive unspecified upfront license fees and could receive additional fees, milestone payments and royalties on products that may result from the collaboration, Lilly said.

In addition, Cambridge will receive rights to develop antibody-based therapeutics to certain selected targets provided by Lilly. As part of the agreement, Lilly said it will also make an unspecified equity investment in Cambridge.

Cambridge is working on ways to rapidly isolate human monoclonal antibodies as a way of speeding the discovery of new drugs. The company's technology could be especially valuable in genomics and in the development of antibody-based human therapeutic products, said Lilly, a major drugmaker.
